context: Current closing price of Monster Beverage (MNST): $91.02 USD as of 2026-08-10.
justification_text:
The point estimates for each horizon—1 day, 1 week, and 1 month—are based on an expectation of gradual progression influenced by underlying factors that I anticipated would drive the trend at each respective time frame. For the 1-day estimate (91.1), I relied largely on the current trajectory of observations and short-term momentum. These sorts of predictions often hinge on stability in recent data and assume no significant deviations in the very near term. By one week (91.5), the point estimate reflects not only the short-term trend but also the incorporation of slightly broader influences that could arise in a medium-term window, such as market adjustments or reactions to new information. By one month (92.3), the point estimate displayed a modest upward adjustment, reflecting the longer-term possibility of gradual shifts in factors like policy, macroeconomic conditions, or broader systemic trends that tend to play out more slowly.

The width of the confidence intervals (CIs) at each horizon reflects the expected uncertainty at those points in time. Over a 1-day time frame, uncertainty is typically low because fewer variables have time to meaningfully shift, so the range of possible outcomes (i.e., 90.36 to 91.84) is narrow. By one week, there is more room for variability as new events or trends may begin to emerge and influence outcomes, thus slightly widening the CI (89.75 to 93.25). At the one-month horizon, a variety of potential unknowns come into play, from economic data releases to geopolitical risks, which widen the range further (88.4 to 96.2). The larger interval accounts for the cumulative effect of many smaller uncertainties, as well as the possibility of larger, less predictable events.

There are specific risks or events that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals, especially at the longer horizons. For instance, a sudden economic shock, such as a policy shift or an unexpected geopolitical event, could cause results to deviate significantly from those predicted. Similarly, the emergence of new data or trends—like stronger-than-expected market sentiment or unanticipated headwinds—may not have been fully accounted for in the model’s assumptions. Even over shorter time frames, unexpected news or volatility spikes could trigger outcomes just outside the stated confidence intervals. These intervals are designed to capture most possibilities (90% of cases in this case), but they can't predict outlier events or extreme outcomes with certainty.
